claims.text: The anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is primarily governed by intrinsic lattice distortions.
Temperature-dependent thermal-expansion mismatch creates internal stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
The mismatch-induced internal stresses interact with dislocation dynamics.
Internal stresses caused by thermal-expansion mismatch promote nanoscale precipitate evolution.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is single-phase BCC.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr possesses inherent chemical short-range order.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr possesses local lattice distortions.
A minor Cr addition can be used to reduce the thermal-expansion mismatch of HfNbTaTiZr.
Differential thermal expansion among constituent atomic species produces localized lattice mismatch as temperature rises.
Thermal expansion at finite temperature can affect lattice parameters and elastic bulk modulus.
Mismatch-generated internal stresses enhance work hardening.
Nanoscale precipitation can affect deformation behavior and plasticity at elevated temperature.
The standard alloy will have greater tensile strength at elevated temperatures than a modified alloy with reduced thermal-expansion mismatch.
The standard alloy will have higher work-hardening rates than the modified alloy at elevated temperatures.
The standard alloy will show more pronounced temperature-dependent shifts in elastic moduli than the modified alloy.
Differences between the standard and modified alloys will be minimal below 600 °C.
Thermal-expansion-mismatch effects will dominate HfNbTaTiZr behavior between 600 and 1250 °C.
Oxidation must be controlled because refractory high-entropy alloys are vulnerable to oxidation and oxidation behavior depends on composition and test conditions.
The proposed comparison assumes that thermal-expansion mismatch can be changed without otherwise changing the alloy microstructure.
A lack of significant differences in both mechanical responses and internal-stress indicators between the standard and modified alloys would falsify the proposed thermal-expansion-mismatch mechanism.
